summary: Two independent fixes to the managed Peloton OAuth path. (1) managedPelotonAccessToken() previously only tried bootstrapPelotonToken() (fresh username/password login) when the persisted bundle had no refresh_token at all; a refresh attempt that itself failed (dead/rotated/revoked refresh_token) returned immediately with no recovery, even with PELOTON_OAUTH_USERNAME/PASSWORD configured. It now falls back to bootstrapPelotonToken() on a refresh failure too, when bootstrap credentials are available -- but never lets the fresh bootstrap response fall back to the old (already-dead) refresh_token if it omits its own. (2) pelotonTwoXXRoundTripper previously masked ANY non-2xx response (redirects and ordinary 4xx/5xx alike) into a generic 'must be 2xx' error, discarding the real status code before client.Client.do() could build its usual *client.APIError -- which made every one of tools.go's status-specific error messages (matched via strings.Contains(err.Error(), "HTTP 403") etc.) unreachable for any managed-Peloton-auth request. It now only intercepts 3xx (the actual gap: do()'s own success check treats any status < 400 as success, so an unfollowed redirect would otherwise be handed to the caller as if it were real API data); 4xx/5xx pass through untouched to do()'s existing, already-correct status-code-aware handling. A regen touching either function must preserve both behaviors -- confirmed via TestManagedCatalogRejectsNon2xxWithoutRetry (redirect still caught) and TestManagedCatalogPreservesRealStatusCodeFor4xx (4xx passes through with real status).
reason: Investigated cross-session: a long-running peloton-pp-mcp container (streamable-HTTP transport, not the CLI's per-invocation lifecycle) had a stale oauth-token.json for over a week -- every live-API tool call failed with the OAuth token endpoint's own error verbatim: "managed Peloton OAuth request failed with HTTP 403", no other detail. Traced to Auth0 rejecting the container's specific refresh_token (most likely rotation/invalidation from running the Mac CLI and this container concurrently against the same Peloton login, each with an independently-persisted token bundle) -- confirmed the refresh-eligibility check itself runs fresh on every single MCP request (not gated to CLI-only lifecycle, refuting that as a cause), so the real gap was the missing bootstrap fallback. The roundtripper status-masking (2) is a related, independently real gap found while tracing the failure path, not the actual cause of this specific report.
validated_outcome: go build/vet/test and verify_skill.py all green. New tests: TestManagedPelotonAccessTokenFallsBackToBootstrapWhenRefreshTokenIsDead, TestManagedPelotonAccessTokenReturnsOriginalRefreshErrorWithoutBootstrapCreds (the exact live scenario: no bootstrap creds configured, original refresh error must survive), TestManagedPelotonAccessTokenKeepsOriginalRefreshErrorWhenBootstrapAlsoFails, TestManagedCatalogPreservesRealStatusCodeFor4xx. Not yet validated against the live container that reported the bug -- unit-tested only as of this entry.
